findings.title: A busy transport can discard the required disconnect command.
findings.trigger: A signaling queue overflow or timeout occurs while the send callback returns busy.
findings.cause: blec_fail calls blec_command once. A failed send does not set waiting or preserve the command. BLEC_DISCONNECTING does not retry.
findings.observed: The transport recovers after 1 ms. No disconnect command reaches it before the 3-second deadline. The host changes to BLEC_FAILED and retains conn=0x50.
findings.first_failed_invariant: The abort must send one disconnect command when the transport recovers before the deadline.
findings.failure: Both overflow and timeout probes fail assert(disconnects == 1). Each process returns -6. Each probe records one rejected attempt and zero accepted disconnects.
findings.impact: The new reply queue cannot guarantee its stated abort behavior under the backpressure condition that it supports. The controller can retain its link while the host reports failure.
findings.provenance_limit: The one-shot blec_fail helper also exists on the base. The new signaling paths call it. This is an exposed dependency defect, not proof of a new original-input regression.
findings.production_transport: ble_send returns xb_frame_put directly. The ring API can return -1 when space is unavailable. The probe substitutes this return condition.
findings.physical_limit: The test does not prove saturation of the physical 1024-byte h2c ring. It does not establish how often this condition occurs.
findings.disposition: Block stage 4. Use one fresh stage 2 for a bounded disconnect retry. Then use a fresh stage 3 for affected checks.
acceptance_criteria: Both overflow and timeout must preserve the pending abort if its first command send fails.
When the transport recovers before the deadline, send exactly one accepted COP_DISCONNECT for the active handle.
Do not repeat an accepted command on later polls.
Do not extend the bounded deadline on each rejected send.
A successful disconnect event must clear pending fragments and replies, restore credits, and permit reconnection.
Keep failed-disconnect events and permanent transport failure distinct from successful disconnection.
Preserve identifiers, reply ordering, ATT limits, MIDI receive behavior, model guards, features, licensing, and budgets.

protocol_review.result: No additional confirmed defect in the selected signaling policy.
observations: CID 5 carries LE signaling. One signaling packet is permitted per C-frame.
Responses retain the request identifier. Identifier zero is invalid.
An unsolicited identified response can be discarded without a reply.
A parameter-update refusal is permitted. Acceptance would require delivery of the parameters to the controller.
The 64-byte signaling MTU exceeds the 23-byte minimum. An oversized request receives the supported MTU.
HCI disconnection frees unacknowledged packets for that handle. The sole-link credit reset follows this rule.

shared_state_review.result: No additional confirmed race in the new fields.
observations: ble_central_service calls blec_rx, blec_poll, blec_start and blec_stop in TIMER5.
The new signaling queue has four entries. Its indices, counters, deadline and ACL assembly fields stay in that context.
The main loop produces the existing MIDI feedback queue through blec_midi_send. It does not write the new signaling fields.
The queue gates ATT and feedback sends until pending signaling replies drain.
ACL assembly retains at most 64 bytes. The uint16_t counters can drain a 65535-byte signaling PDU without a proportional allocation.
Completed-packet addition saturates before uint8_t conversion. A failed disconnect event does not restore credits.
shared_state_review.limit: Source ownership review does not emulate target interrupt timing, stack execution, radio execution or cache behavior.

original_input_failure.owner_evidence: ALL SMC controls fail while light feedback works. The owner confirmed Controls now work and and smc drives them too on reference 53d5654c9bbaec10b64c55fb60d0e7d857ba8156.
observations: The working reference lacks both signaling replies and disconnect-credit reclamation.
The prior idle trace is CONNECTED with handles 114/115, five credits, no pending ATT, no mailbox drops, and continued polling.
Its rejected header is 50 20 10 00 0c 00 05 00. No signaling command or identifier survives.
Zero idle input counters do not prove input loss.
The credit defect reproduces reconnect discovery starvation. That result does not match the CONNECTED observation.
The recorded notification capture contains no correlated session negotiation or physical input transmission during the failure.
Prior target inspection shows PB=2 starts, PB=1 continuations and exact callback lengths for the inspected controller routine.
Prior host comparisons decode the supported unchanged payload stream through startup and the production callback. They do not test physical delivery.
original_input_failure.disposition: Carry the unresolved physical failure forward. Do not infer a complete cure from the abort repair, replay, build, or install.
